units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
The world is simply divided into two classes—those who believe the incredible, like the public—and those who do the improbable—
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Like yourself?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Yes; I am always astonishing myself. It is the only thing that makes life worth living.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: And what have you been doing lately that astonishes you?
units.name: LADY STUTFIELD

units.text: I have been discovering all kinds of beautiful qualities in my own nature.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Ah! don’t become quite perfect all at once. Do it gradually!
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I don’t intend to grow perfect at all. At least, I hope I shan’t. It would be most inconvenient. Women love us for our defects. If we have enough of them, they will forgive us everything, even our gigantic intellects.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It is premature to ask us to forgive analysis. We forgive adoration; that is quite as much as should be expected from us.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Enter LORD ALFRED.
He joins LADY STUTFIELD.
Ah! we women should forgive everything, shouldn’t we, dear Mrs. Arbuthnot? I am sure you agree with me in that.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: I do not, Lady Hunstanton. I think there are many things women should never forgive.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What sort of things?
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: The ruin of another woman’s life.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Moves slowly away to back of stage .

Ah! those things are very sad, no doubt, but I believe there are admirable homes where people of that kind are looked after and reformed, and I think on the whole that the secret of life is to take things very, very easily.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: The secret of life is never to have an emotion that is unbecoming.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: The secret of life is to appreciate the pleasure of being terribly, terribly deceived.
units.name: LADY STUTFIELD

units.text: The secret of life is to resist temptation, Lady Stutfield.
units.name: KELVIL

units.text: There is no secret of life. Life’s aim, if it has one, is simply to be always looking for temptations. There are not nearly enough. I sometimes pass a whole day without coming across a single one. It is quite dreadful. It makes one so nervous about the future.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Shakes her fan at him .
I don’t know how it is, dear Lord Illingworth, but everything you have said to-day seems to me excessively immoral. It has been most interesting, listening to you.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: All thought is immoral. Its very essence is destruction. If you think of anything, you kill it. Nothing survives being thought of.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I don’t understand a word, Lord Illingworth. But I have no doubt it is all quite true. Personally, I have very little to reproach myself with, on the score of thinking. I don’t believe in women thinking too much. Women should think in moderation, as they should do all things in moderation.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Moderation is a fatal thing, Lady Hunstanton. Nothing succeeds like excess.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I hope I shall remember that. It sounds an admirable maxim. But I’m beginning to forget everything. It’s a great misfortune.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: It is one of your most fascinating qualities, Lady Hunstanton. No woman should have a memory. Memory in a woman is the beginning of dowdiness. One can always tell from a woman’s bonnet whether she has got a memory or not.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: How charming you are, dear Lord Illingworth. You always find out that one’s most glaring fault is one’s most important virtue. You have the most comforting views of life.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Enter FARQUHAR.
Doctor Daubeny’s carriage!
units.name: FARQUHAR

units.text: My dear Archdeacon! It is only half-past ten.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Rising .
I am afraid I must go, Lady Hunstanton. Tuesday is always one of Mrs. Daubeny’s bad nights.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: Rising .
Well, I won’t keep you from her.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Goes with him towards door .
I have told Farquhar to put a brace of partridge into the carriage. Mrs. Daubeny may fancy them.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: It is very kind of you, but Mrs. Daubeny never touches solids now. Lives entirely on jellies. But she is wonderfully cheerful, wonderfully cheerful. She has nothing to complain of.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: Exit with LADY HUNSTANTON.
Goes over to LORD ILLINGWORTH.
There is a beautiful moon to-night.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Let us go and look at it. To look at anything that is inconstant is charming nowadays.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You have your looking-glass.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: It is unkind. It merely shows me my wrinkles.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Mine is better behaved. It never tells me the truth.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Then it is in love with you.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH
